cards.design_implication: If the experimental design aims to modulate the electronic or optical properties of a 2D semiconductor, consider implementing one or more of these specific tuning mechanisms as controlled variables.
does_not_establish: Quantitative tunability ranges for specific materials.
Optimal parameter settings for any single mechanism.
Experimental protocols for implementing these mechanisms.
cards.evidence_excerpt: In particular, these 2D materials were demonstrated to exhibit highly tunable bandgaps, achieved via the control of layers number, heterostructuring, strain engineering, chemical doping, alloying, intercalation, substrate engineering, as well as an external electric field.
limitations: This is an abstract-level summary of a review, not a primary experimental report.
The excerpt lists methods generally without specifying material composition or device architecture constraints.
cards.statement: Bandgap tunability in two-dimensional materials is achieved via techniques including the control of layer number, heterostructuring, strain engineering, chemical doping, alloying, intercalation, substrate engineering, and the application of an external electric field.

cards.design_implication: When selecting a 2D material for a device targeting a specific spectral range, verify if the known bandgap ranges of candidate materials (graphene, TMDs, hBN, etc.) align with the target frequency.
does_not_establish: Precise bandgap values for specific samples.
Suitability of these materials for specific device applications beyond general spectral range.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Beyond graphene, recently discovered two-dimensional (2D) materials possess semiconducting bandgaps ranging from the terahertz and mid-infrared in bilayer graphene and black phosphorus, visible in transition metal dichalcogenides, to the ultraviolet in hexagonal boron nitride.
limitations: Broad categorization of materials and spectral ranges.
Abstract-level overview; does not provide detailed band structure calculations or experimental validation data.
cards.statement: Beyond graphene, recently discovered two-dimensional materials possess semiconducting bandgaps ranging from the terahertz and mid-infrared (e.g., bilayer graphene and black phosphorus) through the visible (e.g., transition metal dichalcogenides) to the ultraviolet (e.g., hexagonal boron nitride).
